title: Actual coefficient limits, finite powers, and compatible finite-projective complex retracts
statement: Let X be any scheme and d an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Form the diagram of finite coefficient modules restricted along the actual completed-ring projections, with the recorded quotient maps. The completed coefficient unit, with its original projections, is an ordinary module-sheaf limit of this diagram. Every consecutive coefficient module map is epimorphic. The degree-zero complex tower therefore has the localized completed coefficient unit as its Roos derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit], for every choice of its existing derived product. No geometric hypotheses, coefficient completeness or boundedness hypothesis is required. More generally, finite powers of the coefficient cone are limits with epimorphic transitions. A specified cone of a complex tower whose diagram and cone in every degree are compatibly split retracts of those finite-power coefficient diagrams is an ordinary limit and localizes to a Roos derived limit. The ranks may depend on the degree; no boundedness is needed for this assertion.

source.place: Tag 09C6, the coefficient-unit case of the finite-projective inverse-limit calculation; Cohomology on Sites, Tags 0940/0941; Modules on Sites, Tag 03DA.

proof.text: View each actual completed-ring projection as a linear map from the completed coefficient unit to the restricted quotient unit. The defining ring limit identities give a cone. Forget to module presheaves, evaluate on every object, and forget to additive groups. Identify the resulting diagram and cone with the corresponding forgetful image of the defining ring limit. Preservation and reflection of limits proves the module cone is limiting.

A quotient map of powers is surjective. Choose a set section of its universe lift. Finite quotient rings have the discrete topology, so postcomposition with this section lifts every continuous coefficient function. Sheafification preserves local surjectivity. The specified module transition has exactly those functions on sections; its underlying additive sheaf map is locally surjective, hence epi. Faithful forgetting reflects epi.
The degree-zero single-complex functor preserves limits and epimorphisms. Apply the proved epimorphic complex-tower Roos theorem to the image of the actual coefficient limit cone.

Finite powers preserve limits and finite colimits by the finite biproduct comparison. For a compatible split retract cone, include a test cone into the finite-free diagram, lift into its computed limit, and project. The compatibility and splitting equations prove the universal property. Each retract transition is epi, since after precomposition with its split projection it is the epi free transition followed by a split projection.

For a complex tower with these compatible retracts degree by degree, evaluation jointly reflects limits of complexes. Apply the epimorphic-complex Roos theorem to this ordinary complex limit, whose transitions are epi in every degree.

theorem finitePerfectAdicProjectiveComplex_roos (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A]
    (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules X d) ℤ) (c : Cone T)
    (h : ∀ j : ℤ, Nonempty (FinitePerfectAdicCoefficientRetract X d
      (T ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval (CompletedAdicModules X d) (.up ℤ) j)
      ((HomologicalComplex.eval (CompletedAdicModules X d) (.up ℤ) j).mapCone c))) :
    HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj (op n))) ∧
    ∀ [HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj (op n)))],
      IsDerivedLimit (K := fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj (op n)))
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.map (T.map (homOfLE n.le_succ).op))
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj c.pt)
